Alexandre Déramé
Alexandre Déramé, Domaine du Moulin, Muscadet Sèvre-et-Maine, Sur Lie
2024
0 cs
Near Nantes, west of Mouzillon-Tillières in Saint-Fiacre-sur-Maine, Domaine du Moulin’s Melon de Bourgogne vines were planted in 1991 at 60 meters altitude on shallow (~30 cm) fine-grained sandy topsoil, derived from the granite and schist bedrock below. Whole-cluster pressed, settled overnight, and racked off the sediments, it undergoes natural fermentation in steel tanks and is blocked from malolactic fermentation. The first sulfite addition occurs after primary fermentation, and the wine is filtered with diatomaceous earth (a natural product) before bottling the following spring.
Alexandre Déramé
Alexandre Déramé, La Morandière, Muscadet Sèvre-et-Maine, Sur Lie
2024
0 cs
La Morandière is located on the eastern side of Muscadet Sèvre et Maine, in Mouzillon-Tillières, near Déramé’s top cru, Clos des Roches Gaudenières. The vines, planted at 60 meters altitude, grow on a gently sloping parcel with 80 cm of sandy and silty topsoil, likely derived from the underlying gabbro bedrock—a hard, pale green-black igneous rock, rich in magnesium and iron, formed from the slow cooling of basaltic magma beneath the earth’s surface. Whole-cluster pressed, settled overnight, and racked off the sediments, it undergoes natural fermentation in steel tanks and is blocked from malolactic fermentation. The first sulfite addition occurs after primary fermentation, and the wine is filtered with diatomaceous earth (a natural product) before bottling the following spring.

Alexandre Déramé
Alexandre Déramé, Muscadet Sèvre-et-Maine, Vieilles Vignes, Les Roches Gaudinières
2019
0 cs
The 3-hectare Clos des Roches Gaudenières vineyard, located in Mouzillon-Tillières, sits on the eastern side of Muscadet Sèvre et Maine. A mix of massale selections and old biotypes, it was planted in 1941 and 1971 at 60 meters altitude. The rocky clay topsoil, approximately 80 cm deep, rests on gabbro bedrock, a dense, pale green-black rock formed from the slow cooling of basaltic magma and enriched with magnesium and iron. Whole-cluster pressed, settled overnight, and racked off the sediments before undergoing a natural fermentation in steel tanks. Malolactic is blocked and the first sulfite addition occurs after primary fermentation. It is then aged for two years in porcelain-lined concrete vats, followed by filtration with diatomaceous earth (a natural product) before bottling.

Egia
Alfredo Egia, Bizkaiko Txakolina, Rebel Rebel
2020
0 cs
Bizkaiko has Atlantic & continental influence (greater temp fluctuations than coastline). 4.3ha w/2.8ha Hondarrabi Zerratia/Petit Courbu & 1.5ha Izkiriota Txikia/Petit Manseng. Most topsoil in shallower upper sections likely from bedrock below; further down, deeper soils (avg. ~80cm), more organic matter content. Bedrock (\'cayuela\'), calcareous marl w/slate-like layered appearance, sits nearly vertical, alternating w/siliceous sandstones. Vines planted between 2001-2006. Elev. 200-300m. S exposure. Steep slope. Hand harvest, 100% stem inclusion, direct press, natural ferment, barrels. Malolactic usually overlaps w/end of alcoholic ferment, completed end of spring. Wines sur-lie (no bâttonage); some barrels topped up, others intentionally oxidized/not topped up - depending on health of oxidation. No SO2.

Arnaud Lambert
Arnaud Lambert, Saumur Blanc, La Rue
2019
0 cs
Lambert’s Saumur “Rue” is 100% Chenin Blanc planted between 1970-1995 at 60-80m on white tuffeau limestone bedrock with a topsoil of 25cm of sand, 10cm of clay. It faces south/southwest and is the warmest Chenin Blanc vineyard in Lambert’s Brézé range. Whole cluster pressed after 4.5 hours of skin maceration. First 25% and last 30 minutes of the press juice are declassified and blended into entry-level appellation wines. Natural fermentation in 20% new and 80% 1-5-year-old French oak barrels with a max. temperature of 20C. Malolactic may happen in certain tanks/barrels with a max. of 20%. Bâtonnage may be made at the end of primary fermentation until dry. SO2 is only added just prior to bottling. Aged in 20% new and 80% old (1-5 year old) French oak barrels for 24 months, followed by 6 months in stainless steel before bottling.

Lambert’s Saumur “Clos Mazurique” is 100% Cabernet Franc from the coldest red grape site in Lambert’s range. Lambert’s Clos de l’Étoile is 100% Cabernet Franc planted 35 years ago at 80m on a mild slope facing southwest on 100cm of red sand and loam topsoil on tuffeau limestone bedrock. Destemmed and fermented in concrete for 3 weeks with the first 3-4 days a single pump over and remaining weeks a gentle wetting of cap, at 24°C max. 24 months in 20% new and 80% 1-2-year-old 225L French oak, and 5-6 months in steel. Sulfites added only at bottling. Aged 24 months 20% new and 80% in one and two year old French oak 225-liter barrels. Rack after malolactic; no other racking until bottling. 5-6 months in stainless before bottling.

Lambert’s Saumur “Tue-Loup” is 100% Cabernet Franc comes from 3 parcels planted 35 years ago (2021) at 80m on a mild slope facing southwest with white tuffeau limestone bedrock and 70-80cm of sand and silt topsoil. Destemmed and fermented in concrete tanks with 2/3 8-10 days (first 3-4 days, two pumpovers per day, then 1/day), 1/3 20 days of infusion with max. temperatures at 24C. SO2 added at bottling. SO2 is only added just prior to bottling. Aged in 2/3 in 2-to-3 year old barrels for 10 months. 1/3 aged 10 months in concrete eggs. Barrels are micro-oxygenated and concrete aged wines are racked. Blended six months in stainless steel tanks before bottling, which usually takes place in December.

Continental climate with light precipitation due to the rain shadow effect of the Massif Armorican located toward the west. Winters are mild and summers can be dry and these days quite hot, depending on the year. Vines, 5ha (4ha planted in 1970; 1ha planted in 2017). Elev. 50-70 m. Southern Exposure. Mild to flat slope. 100% stem inclusion, pressed for 4.5 hours. Juice is selected with the first 25% of the press juice and the last 30 minutes of the press juice declassified. Fermentation is natural . Max fermentation temperature 17¬∞C during the one month fermentation. Malolactic fermentation: Max 30%.. Batonnage is made toward the end of the primary fermentation and for some months after the wine is dry. The first SO2 addition is made just before bottling. 90% in stainless steel and 10% old French oak barrels (7+ years old); new experiments are made in concrete eggs. Lightly filtered.

Alberto Oggero
Alberto Oggero, Roero Bianco, Arneis
2024
0 cs
Arneis is drawn from two vineyard parcels: 80% from a south-facing site and 20% from a southeast-facing site, with an average vine age of 20 years, planted on extremely steep, sandy calcareous hillsides at 280 meters of altitude. The south-facing parcel is destemmed and gently pressed, while the southeast-facing parcel is destemmed and lightly crushed before fermentation. Fermentation takes place in stainless steel with each parcel vinified separately. The wines are then aged separately in concrete on fine lees through the winter without racking or bâtonnage. In the spring, they are racked, blended, and bottled. A light filtration is carried out prior to bottling, with no fining.

Alberto Oggero, Roero Nebbiolo, "Anime"

0 cs
Roero “Anime” is harvested from 100-year-old Nebbiolo vines (2026) planted on a southwest exposure on extremely steep calcareous sandy and clay soils at 320 meters of altitude. Anime is softly destemmed using an Oscillys destemmer and fermented with daily pump-overs, followed by continued maceration under submerged cap at the end of fermentation. It is then aged for 12 months in large oak casks and tonneaux, followed by 6 months in concrete, and is bottled without fining or filtration.

Rafanelli Winery
Rafanelli Cabernet
2022
0 cs
This was one of the driest years on record. The lack of rainfall produced lighter berries and smaller clusters. The steep hillsides provide for great drainage and shading necessary to produce Cabernet Sauvignon. Harvested on Sept 5th with 24-25 Brix ABV 14.5% The sustainably farmed grapes are harvested off the hillside by hand, and then brought to the winery where they are sorted, crushed, and fermented. Fermentation takes place in small open top tanks. Here the cap is punched down manually four times a day to obtain the dark color, rich flavors and tannin balance. After fermentation is complete, the new wine is lightly pressed and put into oak barrels.

Rafanelli Winery
Rafanelli Zinfandel
2022
0 cs
100% Estate Vineyards from both sides of the Dry Creek Valley. A dry winter with rains decreasing after the first of January. The spring brought windy conditions causing shatter in the young clusters. Minimal rainfall produced lower yields, leading to intense color and flavors. Above normal temperatures jumpstarted the harvest and all the fruit was picked betore the record heat wave. The grapes are hand harvested, then brought to the winery where they are hand sorted, crushed, and fermented. Fermentation takes place in small open top tanks. 22 months in new, one and two year old French Oak. No Fining or filtration.

Close to Cabe river, little further away toward E, eastern side S facing amphitheater. Parcel abuts indigenous tree grove, E flank, providing cooling affect from heat. Mencía, Garnacha & other varieties. Heavily decomposed granite bedrock, medium-grain, sandy topsoil entirely of granite derived from bedrock. Vines planted ~1942. Elev. 300m. S exposure. Very steep slope. 90% stem inclusion, gentle extraction, quasi-infusion (cap only wetted 2x/day). Natural ferment, open-top 1000L fermenters, on skins 1 mo., then pressing. Malolactic old oak barrel. 1st SO2 added at harvest - depends on fruit.

Harvested from a 1.1-hectare plot north of Portonovo in Val do Salnés 2.5 kilometers from Atlantic. Sulfites added just prior to bottling.

Rafanelli Winery
Rafanelli Cabernet
2021
0 cs
This was one of the driest years on record. The lack of rainfall produced lighter berries and smaller clusters. The steep hillsides provide for great drainage and shading necessary to produce Cabernet Sauvignon. Harvested on Sept 5th with 24-25 Brix ABV 14.5% The sustainably farmed grapes are harvested off the hillside by hand, and then brought to the winery where they are sorted, crushed, and fermented. Fermentation takes place in small open top tanks. Here the cap is punched down manually four times a day to obtain the dark color, rich flavors and tannin balance. After fermentation is complete, the new wine is lightly pressed and put into oak barrels.

0.38ha, La Capella, steep vineyard (45 degrees). Mostly Pinot Meunier (Chardonnay & Pinot Gris interplanted). Vines are dense, 5000-6000 ft/ha. Positioned to experience some of the most intense & direct winds w/in valley. Deep layers of clay cover chalky subsoils at bottom of slope; silex, marne & limestone dominate upper slope (some sections just 10cm topsoil). SE exposure. Hand harvested when 11-12 °C. Gentle press, natural ferment, tonneaux. Bâttonage regularly during winter months. SO2 levels (12-37 mg/L), added just before bottling.

Chateau de Breze, Saumur Blanc, 'Clos de la Rue'
2013
0 cs
Lambert’s Saumur “Rue” is 100% Chenin Blanc planted between 1970-1995 at 60-80m on white tuffeau limestone bedrock with a topsoil of 25cm of sand, 10cm of clay. It faces south/southwest and is the warmest Chenin Blanc vineyard in Lambert’s Brézé range. Whole cluster pressed after 4.5 hours of skin maceration. First 25% and last 30 minutes of the press juice are declassified and blended into entry-level appellation wines. Natural fermentation in 20% new and 80% 1-5-year-old French oak barrels with a max. temperature of 20C. Malolactic may happen in certain tanks/barrels with a max. of 20%. Bâtonnage may be made at the end of primary fermentation until dry. SO2 is only added just prior to bottling.

Lambert’s Saumur “Rue” is 100% Chenin Blanc planted between 1970-1995 at 60-80m on white tuffeau limestone bedrock with a topsoil of 25cm of sand, 10cm of clay. It faces south/southwest and is the warmest Chenin Blanc vineyard in Lambert’s Brézé range. Whole cluster pressed after 4.5 hours of skin maceration. First 25% and last 30 minutes of the press juice are declassified and blended into entry-level appellation wines. Natural fermentation in 20% new and 80% 1-5-year-old French oak barrels with a max. temperature of 20C. Malolactic may happen in certain tanks/barrels with a max. of 20%. Bâtonnage may be made at the end of primary fermentation until dry. SO2 is only added just prior to bottling.

Cume do Avia, Ribeiro Branco, Arraiano
2022
0 cs
Arraiano Blanco comes from Treixadura (80%), Albariño, Loureiro, and a small quantity of Godello planted between 1995-2010 at elevations of 110-160 on south-facing exposures. The majority of the vines are older and sit at an altitude of 110–160m on south-facing, unterraced, medium-steep slopes over a mix of metamorphic (schist, slate, gneiss) and igneous (granite, granodiorite) bedrock, with a topsoil mix of very rocky sand, silt, and clay. Arraiano Blanco goes through a natural fermentation with maximum temperatures between 18-23°C in steel and are aged 5 months in large, ancient (restored) chestnut foudres. Before bottling, it is lightly filtered.

Cume do Avia, Ribeiro Tinto, Arraiano
2020
0 cs
Arraiano Tinto is principally Caíño Longo, Brancellao, and Sousón, with about 20% other indigenous varieties. The vines, planted between 2003-2008 sit around 140 m on mid-slope sites over igneous (granite, granodiorite) and metamorphic (slate, schist) bedrock, with red and brown clay- and sand-rich topsoils derived from the parent rock. Arraiano Tinto is 40% whole cluster natural “infusion” fermentation over 2-3 weeks at 28°C (maximum) and 9 months of aging mostly in steel (sometimes large restored chestnut foudres). Before bottling, it is lightly filtered.

Christophe, Chablis, Grand Cru Les Preuses
2020
0 cs
One of the two northernmost Grand Crus (the other, Bugros), Les Preuses takes its name from the Roman word for stony road (voie pierreuse, which evolved to la pierreuse, then la preuse) and faces south/southwest at 170-205m above Bugros on a gentler slope than many of the Grand Crus (save Bugros, which may be the gentlest of the grand cru slopes). Like the rest of the Grand Crus, the topsoil is marne (limestone-rich clay) and marl-rich topsoil (but here a mix of white and brown clay), on Kimmeridgian limestone marl bedrock. Hand harvested, pressed, and settled overnight, then racked off heavy sediments before undergoing a slow, low temperature, natural fermentation over 1-2 months prior to a year of aging in 80-85% steel and 15-20% in 228L oak barrels (new, 1-, 2-, and 3-year-old) with an occasional bâttonage, if needed. Prior to bottling it\'s fined and filtered.

Giraudière’s Saumur Blanc “L\'Ardillon de Brézé” is Chenin Blanc from vines planted in Brézé in 1985, 2003, and 2009, at 75 meters of altitude on a gentle slope facing north-south and east-west, depending on the parcel. The topsoil is deep clay with limestone and flint rock on limestone bedrock. Saumur Blanc “L\'Ardillon de Brézé” is fermented in barrels at a maximum of 17°C and aged for 12 months before bottling. No malolactic fermentation and the first sulfites are added after vinification and again at bottling. The wine is filtered.

Rousset’s Crozes-Hermitage Blanc Vieille Vignes is 100% Marsanne from vines planted in 1933 and 1965 between Gervans and Erôme on soft/medium steep terraces with mostly south-west expositions at 140-180m on granite and loess bedrock with mostly loess topsoil. Whole-cluster pressed and naturally fermented and aged aged in 10% new French oak and 90% young French oak for 8 months before bottling. It passes through malolactic and is filtered with diatomaceous earth (a natural product) prior to bottling.

Grand 'Cour
Grand' Cour, Brouilly, Cuvée Vieilles Vignes (Dutraive)
2017
0 cs
Located in Jean-Louis’ familial domaine on the eastern end of Brouilly, this unique vineyard is composed of limestone and clay (uncommon in the appellation, where most vines are planted on granite). The vineyard was planted between 1923 and 1973 at altitudes of 250-350 meters, with a south-facing exposure on a gentle slope. 100% whole cluster, semi-carbonic, natural fermentation and maceration for 2-3 weeks and the wine aged in 50% in steel and 50% in old 225 L French oak for 7 months. 10ppm (10mg/L) total added sulfites only at bottling, no fining nor filtration.

Located in the relatively large “Champagne” lieu-dit, just east and downhill across the Rue de la Grappe Fleurie from the family’s Clos de la Grand’Cour vineyard and cellar, this is the Dutraive family’s smallest family-owned parcel at 1.5 hectares. Their plot was planted between 1950 and 1980 at 300 meters on a gentle, east-southeast-facing slope on shallow topsoil (10-30cm deep) consisting of granite sand, derived from its pink granite bedrock. 100% whole cluster, semi-carbonic, natural fermentation and maceration in concrete for 2-3 weeks and the wine aged in old 225-500 L old French oak with ~20% new oak for 7 months. 10ppm (10mg/L) total added sulfites only at bottling, no fining nor filtration.

Collinet
Collinet, Champagne, Extra Brut, Temporis (Disg 11.21)
2014
1.33 cs
While geologically classified as Kimmeridgian, Les Riceys has limestone marl and calcareous mudstones with a more geometric rock appearance than the neighboring flaky, friable, fossil-rich Chablis Kimmeridgian limestone marls. However, more like Chablis and Côte d’Or than the chalky north of Champagne, Les Riceys’s topsoil is rocky with calcareous clay and silt and very little sand. The vineyards also have a greater biodiversity through its many forests that separate its hills when compared to the north of Champagne. “Temporis" is a blend of 98% Pinot Noir and 2% Chardonnay from medium sloping vineyards at 300m with a south/southeast exposure. Whole cluster pressed and naturally fermented in steel. The wine goes through malolactic fermentation. The tirage is made in the spring after harvest and disgorged 5 years after harvest date. The dosage is 4.3g/L and the alcohol is 12.2%.

Oliviero Pastoris
Pastoris, Canavese, Nebbiolo, La Cucca
2021
0 cs
Canavese Nebbiolo "La Cucca” is composed of 100 % Nebbiolo harvested from of a single hectare of terraced plots planted in 1970-1980 at 380-400 meters facing north to south on morainic soils principally composed of white quartz bedrock with a deep sandy, clay and rocky topsoil. Natural fermentation of destemmed Nebbiolo for 60 days in steel at 25°C max with 3 months on skins without any extraction movements. Aged on lees until after malolactic, where it is then racked into cement for 6 more months of aging. I moved the wine only after malolactic and before bottling. Total sulfites of 40-45 mg/L added only after malolactic and before bottling when filtered.
Oliviero Pastoris
Pastoris, Erbaluce di Caluso, La Norezza
2022
1.25 cs
The Erbaluce di Caluso is harvested from of a single hectare of Erbaluce plots planted in 2000-2001, and 2015 at 380-400 meters facing north to south on a medium-steep terraces and gentle hills on morainic soils principally composed of white quartz bedrock with a deep sandy, clay and rocky topsoil. Natural fermentation for 40 days in steel at 25°C max. Aged on lees in steel and sometimes goes through malolactic fermentation. Total sulfites of 40-45 mg/L added only after malolactic and before bottling when filtered.

Áreas de Rei is sourced from 80-year-old vines of Dona Branca, planted on granite bedrock and topsoil at altitudes exceeding 450m in the Monterrei D.O. Natural fermentation in old oak at low temperatures and is aged for 10 months, partially under flor, in ancient 500-600L French and American oak barrels. Sulfites are added only at bottling, and the wine is unfined and unfiltered.

2021
0 cs

Natural fermentation in old oak at low temps. Aged 10 months partially under flor yeast in 50% amphora and 50% in old 500-600l French oak. No fining or filtration.

Augalevada, Ribeiro Tinto, Mercenario
2020
1.08 cs

Saumur blanc comes from 60-year-old Chenin Blanc vines from numerous organically farmed parcels. The topsoil ranges from pure sand, calcareous clay and silex, from exposed and relatively flat vineyards on varying bedrock (tuffeau to silex) at an altitude of 50–90 meters. Directly pressed, settled overnight and naturally fermented at ambient temperatures (typically a maximum of 20°C, but not controlled) in small raw concrete tanks of varying capacities to vinify each parcel separately. Aging takes place in tank for 6 to 9 months. A light filtration is carried out prior to bottling, with no fining.

Berrye’s Saumur Blanc, “Les Bourgères” is a Chenin Blanc harvested from vines planted in 1993 on gentle to medium-sloped, south-facing plots at 80-100 meters altitude (30-50 meters higher than the average of Saumur and Saumur-Champigny) on white tuffeau limestone bedrock with a relatively thin topsoil of calcareous silt, sand and clay. Natural fermentation in concrete & old 225-400-liter wood casks with further aging in the same vessels for a minimum of one year, depending on each season. Malolactic happens but is not intended nor intentionally discouraged. The first sulfites are added at bottling where it is also lightly filtered.

Planted on a rocky terroir of ancient alluvium from the Massif Central, these fifty-year-old vines (2025) are situated at an altitude of 260 meters. 100% whole cluster, semi-carbonic, natural fermentation and maceration, the grapes were vinified in concrete and the wine aged for 7 months in old French oak. 10ppm (10mg/L) total added sulfites only at bottling, no fining nor filtration.

Seoane Novelle (Prádio)
Pradio, Brancellao
2019
0 cs
Surrounded by indigenous forests on all sides but the river side and influenced by both oceanic and continental weather, all of Pradio’s vines were planted in the early 2000s on south/southeast-facing terraced slope of granite and schist at 190-240m overlooking the Miño River. Hand harvested, fully destemmed, and naturally fermented for 7-10 days in granite lagars (stone vats). The wine is gravity fed into older French oak barrels (mostly 500L with a few smaller sizes 300L and 225L) prior to pressing the pomace. The wines are usually racked and sulfured after malolactic and again at bottling with a total of between 30-50 ppm of sulfites.

2016
0 cs
Las Quintas is a blend of 100-130-year-old partially own-rooted Mencía (85%), Alicante Bouschet (13%), and Palomino and Doña Blanca (2%) from recently recovered abandoned vineyards now under organic farming. The soils are slate-derived with quartzite cobbles and clay at 850-1000m altitude. 80% whole-cluster natural fermentation in open-top, old French oak barrels and 30-50hl tronconic vats with the initial extracted by foot prior to fermentation followed by hands-off infusion for most of the 28-60 days on skins prior to pressing. It’s aged in non-new French oak barrels. First sulfites are added at crush and the final wine is unfined but lightly filtered.

“Il Bossolo” (named after the nearby hotspring) comes from a .55ha plot planted by Giacomo in 2009 on a medium slope facing northwest at 500-520m on limestone bedrock and a calcareous clay and silt topsoil. 10% whole cluster natural ferment for 25-32 days with 2-3 daily punch downs. Aged 18 months in 228-500l old French oak, full ML, and 6 months in steel. No fining or filtration.

Aged 18 months in 228-500l old French oak, full ML, and 6 months in steel. No fining or filtration.

Aged 18 months in 228-500L old French oak, full ML, and 6 months in steel. No fining or filtration.

“Il Pergola” comes from 0.7ha of a local Grechetto massale selections planted in 2019 on a medium slope facing west at 585-605m on limestone bedrock with a rocky, white clay and silt topsoil. Full skin maceration (destemmed) and natural fermentation for 4-5 wks in vat. Aged 12 months in old 400l French oak and 450l steel drums and then blended and aged 6 months in steel. Full ML. First sulfites prior to fermentation. No fining or filtration.

“L’Affacciatoio” (to look out over something) comes from 0.9ha of massale selection Chardonnay from France’s Côte de Beaune planted in 2019 on a medium slope facing west at 585-600m on limestone bedrock with a rocky, red clay and silt topsoil. Whole cluster pressed, 36 hrs of must settling before natural fermentation and aging in old 400L French oak for 12 months (ML in barrel), and 8 months in steel. First sulfites prior to fermentation. Light filtration.

Jean Collet
Jean Collet, Chablis
2022
0 cs
Located on the Saône left bank, Collet’s Chablis AOC comes from 72 organic certified plots in Villy in the north, the north slope of Montmains across from Vaillons, and Prehy, planted between 1978-1983 on flat to medium-steep slopes at an average of 170m. The bedrock is Kimmeridgian limestone marl with a topsoil of limestone rock, clay and sand. Natural fermentation (13˚C max.) and aging for 11 months in steel. First sulfites added to must, full malolactic, and light fining and filtration.

Located on the Saône left bank, Butteaux comes from the far western side of the Montmains hill from an organic certified plot planted in 1972 facing south/southeast on a medium steep slope at 225-270m. The bedrock is Kimmeridgian limestone marl with a deep topsoil (~50cm) of rich, blue-tinted clay and large and small limestone rock. Natural fermentation and aging for 11 months in steel, followed by 2-3 months in old 228L French oak. First sulfites added to must, full malolactic, and light fining and filtration.

Jardins de Fleury, Chenin Blanc, La Source
2023

Source is 100% Chenin Blanc from a single 0.7-hectare parcel, planted in 2017 at an altitude of 70 m on a flat west-facing slope. The topsoil is a quartz-rich, schist-derived clay over green and black schist bedrock. 2023 Source was whole-cluster pressed and naturally fermented in 30 hl steel tanks for 4 days at 23°C maximum, and underwent full malolactic. It’s aged in 12 hl Tava clay amphoras and old 225L French oak for 8 months before it was bottled with 10 mg/L of total added sulfites, and was not fined, nor filtered.

La Casaccia
La Casaccia, Barbera del Monferrato, Giuanin
2022
0 cs
100% Barbera harvested from vines planted between 2004-2022 on many different hills (because it’s the most versatile and resilient variety) at 160-260 meters on gentle to medium-steep slopes of shallow chalky limestone topsoil on bedrock of clay, chalk, calcareous sandstone, carbonate-rich mudstone, and conglomerate. Giuanin\' is naturally fermented for 2 weeks in steel vats (50-100 hl) at 22-24°C maximum with 2-3 daily gentle pumpovers (like rain, not a stream of wine), then the free-run wine is drawn off (without pressing) to finish fermentation in large steel vats (50-100 hl) at 22-24°C maximum. It’s then aged on fine lees for 2 months, racked off the lees and aged in steel until bottling between June and July. It’s not fined but is filtered before bottling. Sulfites are added during racking and before bottling with a total sulfite range between 30-60ppm, depending on the year.

La Casaccia, Piemonte DOC, Chardonnay, Charno
2023
0 cs
100% Chardonnay harvested from various plots typically planted in 2004-2022 in the middle of the hills between at 190-210 meters facing south and east on gentle to medium-steep slopes of carbonate-rich mudstone and calcareous sandstone, and conglomerate bedrock with a shallow limestone-rich topsoil. Charno\' is for 14 days in steel at 15°C maximum, followed by fine lees aging for 6-8 months in large steel vats (50-100 hl) and rarely goes through malolactic fermentation. It is fined with bentonite (natural clay) before primary fermentation and filtered before bottling (to prevent malolactic in bottle). Sulfites are added in small quantities during racking and before bottling with a total sulfite range between 40-60ppm, depending on the year.
La Casaccia
La Casaccia, Freisa del Monferrato, Monfiorenza
2020
0 cs
100% Freisa harvested from various plots planted in 2006-2013, and because it needs more water, it’s planted on lower portions (because it can manage better mildew pressure because of its thick skins) of each gentle to medium-steep hill at 190-230 meters facing east, south, and north, on chalky limestone and calcareous sandstone bedrock with topsoil derived from the underlying bedrock. Monfiorenza\' is destemmed and naturally fermented in fiberglass tanks for 5-7 days on skins with 2-3 daily gentle pumpovers (like rain, not a stream of wine), then the free-run wine is drawn off (without pressing) to finish fermentation in large steel vats (50-100 hl) at 22-24°C maximum. It’s then aged on fine lees for 2 months, racked off the lees and aged in steel until bottling between May to July. It’s not fined but is filtered before bottling. Sulfites are added during racking and before bottling with a total sulfite range between 30-60ppm, depending on the year.

Leo Steen Wines
Leo Steen, 'Bubbles of Steen' Erewhon UPC Code
2022
0 cs
We found the perfect match in the Clarksburg AVA for our first Sparkling Chenin Blanc. This old vine Chenin Blanc was planted in 1979 on its own root in light well drained sandy soils of the Sacramento River. The 2022 growing season produced an excellent vintage and no exception to the upper Delta region.Hand harvested on August 16th at 18.6 brix with great flavor development and high acidity. Fermentation: Whole cluster pressed on a five hour press cycle for a gentle extraction. The juice was settled in tank for 24 hours before racking to a mix of 10 to 12 year old oak barrels for fermentation. After Indigenous yeast fermentation to complete dryness followed by 10 weeks on the lees in neutral oak before we racked the young wine to tank for blending and shipping. Tirage bottling: This part of the process was done at Rack & Riddle in Healdsburg, with their state of the art triage bottling line for this Traditional Method sparkling Chenin Blanc. After 14 months Sur latte wine was disgorged in December 2023 and corked without any dosage.

The grapes come from a single vineyard in the eastern hills of the Gabilan Mountains, near Monterey Bay and about 20 miles from the Pacific. Soils are rich in decomposed granite with limestone layers at roughly 1,200 ft (365 m). The grapes are gently foot-trodden for a few hours of skin contact to help release nutrients for a healthy fermentation, which took place in a combination of seasoned 400- and 500-liter French oak puncheons using indigenous yeast. The wine aged for 15 months in wood and underwent malolactic fermentation before being racked to stainless steel for two months, then bottled without filtration and with a minimum of added sulfites.

2011
0 cs
After years of searching for just the right Chenin Blanc to work with, I found what I was looking for. The Chenin Blanc vineyard was planted by Saini Farms in 1981 on their Dry Creek Valley property. Yolo sandy loam soils on an old river bottom site, these dry-farmed vines produce grapes that capture the fresh, enticing purity that can be achieved when Chenin Blanc is grown with care and respect. Grapes for our NV SØD is from the cooler and late ripening 2011 vintage. We hand picked the Saini Chenin on September 22nd at 22.1 Brix. After juice settling and racking to tank fermentation started spontaneously. On October 3rd we barreled down the fermenting juice to neutral Burgundy barrels and arrested the fermentation by adding high proof alcohol. At that point alcohol was at 6.4% and 11 Brix in the fermenting tank.

Trans-Douro-Express reds come from numerous vineyards and grape varieties within Douro’s three sub-regions: Douro Superior, the furthest east and the warmest; Baixo Corgo, in the colder western end; and Cima Corgo, in the middle. The vineyards range from steep to extremely steep, with significant variability in exposure and altitude (120-500+ meters). Schist is the predominant bedrock, although some areas also feature intrusive igneous rock (like granite), with loam topsoil mostly derived from the underlying bedrock. Destemmed and spontaneously co-fermented for 4-5 days in a rock lagar and 4000L concrete vats, with a single daily extraction by pumpover or by foot and hand before pressing and aging for 8 months in concrete. The wine is racked as needed, lightly filtered, and sometimes fined prior to bottling.

Menina d'Uva, Vinho Branco, Liquen

Menina d’Uva \'Liquen\' is a blend of 70% Malvasia and 30% other white grapes (Bastardo Branco, Formosa, Poilta), from vines between 40–60 years old (as of 2025), planted at 550 meters on a gentle to medium-steep slope of topsoil derived from the underlying metamorphic (mostly schist) bedrock. Branco is hand-harvested, then gently pressed by foot (with no extended skin contact time) prior to pressing for a natural co-fermentation of all the varieties in steel, with sulfites only added at bottling. It’s aged for 8 months in steel, with the first sulfites added at bottling, without fining or filtration.

Menina d'Uva, Vinho Tinto, Ciste
2021

Menina d’Uva ‘Ciste’ is a blend of more than 15 indigenous red and white grapes (highlighted by Tinta Gorda, Malvasia, Bastardo Preta, Bastardo Branco, Formosa, and Verdelho), planted between 60–80 years ago at 550 meters altitude, on a gentle slope of iron-rich red clay soils derived from acidic metamorphic and igneous rock erosion. Ciste is a destemmed, natural co-fermentation of all the varieties in steel for approximately five days, with variations of pigeage by foot and pumpovers, and pressing at the end of fermentation. It’s aged for 8 months—60% in fiberglass and 40% in very old 228-liter French oak—with the first sulfites added at bottling, without fining or filtration.

A Merced is naturally fermented with 50% whole bunches for 15 days in steel and clay amphora without temperature control, with a light daily cap wetting. It’s then pressed and aged for two winters in old 225- and 500-liter French oak barrels, followed by a light filtration before bottling. Sulfites are added after ML and again at bottling.

Mauro Marengo
Marengo, Barolo, Angela
2019
8.42 cs
Marengo’s Barolo “Angela” comes from numerous younger vine parcels in Terlo and Ravera in the località Novello and Barolo exposed mostly east on a steep slope of calcareous marl, sand and silt between 350-415m. The Barolo “Angela” is naturally fermented with a skin maceration time of 32-35 days with three daily pumpovers in the beginning of fermentation and one or none in the later maceration period. After fermentation, it is racked once or twice prior to going into 25hl botte for 20-22 months and an additional two in steel. It is neither fined nor filtered.

Grüner Veltliner Ried Brandstatt was planted in 2013 in the Wachau’s Spitzer Graben where it sits at 360 meters of altitude on extremely steep terraces with south exposure. The thin topsoil is rich in organic matter and rock and sand derived from the underlying bedrock of gneiss and mica schist. Grüner Veltliner Ried Brandstatt grapes are immediately pressed over an 8-hour cycle, tank settled for 12 hours, and then undergo spontaneous natural fermentation with a maximum temperature of 18-22˚C and continued aging in 600-3000 L steel vats for 10 months. Malolactic rarely happens but is not inhibited, and the first sulfites are added a month after fermentation. The wine is lightly filtered before bottling.

Marengo’s Langhe Nebbiolo comes from numerous young vine parcels (5-25 years old) in the località Novello, Serra, and Zora, including the MGA Ravera’s 20-year-old vines (2023) and the MGA La Volta’s at 68, and Zora, 53, exposed in all directions on gentle (La Volta and Zora) to steep (Ravera) slopes of calcareous marl, sand and silt between 380-430m. The Langhe Nebbiolo is naturally fermented in steel and concrete, and the macerations last about 25-27 days with daily pumpovers: three in the first days and one later into the maceration. Temperatures in steel are controlled while those in concrete are not. After pressing, it’s racked once or twice before going into 10, 25 and 30hl botte for 4-5 months, selected for quality, then racked into steel for another two months before bottling. Sulfites are first added after malolactic, and it’s not fined nor filtered.

OJAI VINEYARD
Ojai, Chardonnay, Santa Barbara County, Clima Frío
2024
0 cs
This wine is sourced from two vineyards. Strange Family Vineyard is a newer planting located up Drum Canyon Road in the Sta. Rita Hills AVA. The 15-year-old vines are planted on steep slopes of pure sand and are farmed organically. The site sits at 400 feet of altitude with a southern exposition on sandy soils. Yellow Foxtrot Vineyard lies west of the Sta. Rita Hills AVA in Cebada Canyon. Planted in 2020 as part of a conservation easement designed to protect wildlife habitat, the vineyard is sustainably farmed with exceptional attention to detail. The vines are planted in sandy soils, heavily influenced by the nearby ocean, with a northern exposition on sand. Fermented with native yeasts and underwent approximately 50% malolactic fermentation in 2024. Aged for 10 months in 228L French oak barrels, with 14% new oak. The first sulfite addition was made at bottling, maintaining minimal effective molecular SO₂.
OJAI VINEYARD
Ojai, Chardonnay, Santa Barbara County, Puerta Del Mar (Special Bottling)
2023
0 cs
This wine comes from 20-year-old Chardonnay vines planted in Santa Barbara County, just west of the Sta. Rita Hills AVA. The vineyard comprises three level acres, densely planted and trained to a narrow vertical trellis. It sits within a bowl-shaped depression with a northern exposition, which helps moderate the climate. The soils consist of clay mixed with rocky alluvial river wash and fragments of white shale, over Monterey shale bedrock. Fermented with native yeasts and underwent approximately 50% malolactic fermentation in 2024. Aged for 10 months in 228L French oak barrels, with 14% new oak. The first sulfite addition was made at bottling, maintaining minimal effective molecular SO₂.

2024
0 cs
Fruit for this wine comes from three vineyards, with an average vine age of 18 years. Presqu’ile Vineyard is located in the Santa Maria Valley AVA at elevations ranging from 700 to 1,000 feet. The soils are sand and sandy loam, and the vineyard is farmed sustainably and SIP Certified. Yellow Foxtrot Vineyard, located west of the Sta. Rita Hills AVA in Cebada Canyon, was planted in 2020 as part of a conservation easement. The vines are planted in sandy soils, heavily influenced by the ocean, with a westerly exposition on oceanic alluvium. Puerta Del Mar Vineyard contributes a small percentage of the blend. The 20-year-old vines are planted just west of the Sta. Rita Hills AVA in Santa Barbara County. The vineyard sits in a bowl-shaped depression that funnels warmth into an otherwise very cold site. The soils include clay, rocky alluvial river wash, and bits of white shale over Monterey shale bedrock and alluvial topsoil. The vineyard is organically farmed (not certified) and sits at 400 feet of altitude with a northerly exposition. Includes 8% whole-cluster fermentation, with one pump-over per day during a 12-day native yeast fermentation. The wine is then pressed and settled in vat for 1 to 2 days before aging for 11 months in older barrels, with 9% new French oak. No fining or filtration. The first sulfite addition of 20 ppm is made at bottling.

This wine comes from 28-year-old vines in the Sta. Rita Hills AVA, planted on steep slopes at 600 feet of altitude with a south-facing exposition. Adam has worked with this vineyard since 2003 and purchased it in 2020, converting it to organic farming in 2021. The soils are Tierra loam (a clay loam series) over fractured shale and sandstone. Fermented with 12.5% whole clusters, using one pump-over per day during a 12-day native yeast fermentation. The wine is pressed and settled in vat for 2 days, then aged for 15 months in 20% new French oak. No fining or filtration. A first sulfite addition of 25 ppm was made in spring 2024, followed by a small addition at bottling on January 25, 2025.

This wine comes from 25-year-old vines located just a few miles west of Los Alamos in the Santa Barbara County AVA. The vineyard is planted on flat to gently rolling sand dunes only a few miles from the Pacific Ocean. The soils are marine-based, consisting of Arnold sand and Betteravia sandy loam over deep alluvial deposits. The vineyard is farmed organically, though not certified. The site sits at 200 feet of altitude with a westerly exposition on oceanic alluvium. Half of the fruit was pressed directly into tank, while the other half was destemmed and allowed five hours of skin contact before pressing. All lots fermented with native yeasts and did not undergo malolactic fermentation. Aged for 11 months in neutral 228L French oak barrels. Bottled with minimal effective molecular SO₂.

2008
0 cs
The Grüner Veltliner Weissenkircher Ried Weitenberg is on south/southwest facing steep terraces at 320m. Planted with ancient massale selection in the early 1950s, the bedrock is orthogneiss and mica schist. Grapes are macerated up to 24 hours (depending on ripeness, with riper grapes receiving less time), then pressed over 6-8 hours, tank settled for a day and naturally fermented at 24˚C max and aged for 9 months in old 1500L Stockinger barrels until spring. Malolactic is completed, and the first sulfites are added between malolactic and bottling. It\'s fined (as most Veltliners are because of their naturally high proteins) but not filtered.

Located in the Wachau’s coldest left bank area, the Spitzer Graben, the Riesling Viesslinger Ried Bruck is on south-facing, steep terraces at 350m. Planted between 1987-2002, the bedrock and topsoil is mica schist. Grapes are macerated up to 24 hours (depending on ripeness, with riper grapes receiving less time), then pressed over 6-8 hours, tank settled for a day and naturally fermented at 24˚C max and aged for 6-8 months in steel. Malolactic is inhibited by low temperatures, and the first sulfites are added at bottling. It\'s filtered but not fined.

The Riesling Schoner is the first picking of slightly botrytised grapes from terraced vineyard sites planted between 1977-2012, including Bruck, Brandstatt, Buschenberg, and Burgstall. At 220-470m altitude, the bedrock and topsoil ranges between mica schist and alluvial sand with numerous south and east exposures. Grapes are macerated up to 24 hours (depending on ripeness, with riper grapes receiving less time), then pressed over 6-8 hours, tank settled for a day and naturally fermented at 24˚C max and aged for 8 months in steel. Malolactic is inhibited by low temperatures, and the first sulfites are added at bottling. It\'s filtered but not fined. The residual sugar ranges between 50-70g/L, depending on the year.

Richoux’s Irancy is 100% Pinot Noir from many different parcels with an average age of 35-40 years (2023) on a medium to steep slopes with a southeast/south/west exposures at 180-280m on limestone marl bedrock and brown clay topsoil. The Grüner Veltliner Alter-Native comes from vines planted in 2012 on the south/southwest-facing, medium-steep terraces of the crus, Buschenberg, Loibenberg and Hochrain. The altitudes range between at altitudes of 260-290m, and the bedrock and topsoil is a mix of loess and mica schist. 95% destemmed natural ferment for 4 weeks in steel with gentle daily punch downs. Aged in small old oak barrels where malolactic takes place with sulfites added only at bottling.
Veyder‐Malberg
Veyder Malberg, Grüner Veltliner, Viessling
2023
0 cs
The Grüner Veltliner “Viessling” comes from vines planted in the Spitzer Graben in 2000 facing directly east on micaschist bedrock and topsoil. All are southerly exposures on either terraces or plateaus between Loiben and Spitz at 200-270m. The soils are principally calcareous loess and river deposits. The grapes are macerated up to 24 hours (depending on ripeness, with riper grapes receiving less time), then pressed over 6-8 hours, tank settled for a day and naturally fermented at 24˚C max and aged in steel and old 300-1500L barrels for 5 months. Malolactic is completed, and the first sulfites are added between malolactic and bottling. It\'s fined and lightly filtered.

2023

The Grüner Veltliner Wösendorfer Hochrain is in western Wachau on south/southwest-facing steep terraces between 260-290m. Planted in 1987-1992, the topsoil is predominantly loess and the bedrock is loess and decomposed paragneiss. Collected over numerous pickings from the same parcel, the grapes are macerated up to 24 hours (depending on ripeness, with riper grapes receiving less time), then pressed over 6-8 hours, tank settled for a day and naturally fermented at 24˚C max and aged 6 months in 1500L Stockinger barrels. Malolactic is completed, and the first sulfites are added between malolactic and bottling. It\'s fined (as most Veltliners are because of their naturally high proteins) but not filtered.

The Riesling Schoner is the first picking of slightly botrytised grapes from terraced vineyard sites planted between 1977-2012, including Bruck, Brandstatt, Buschenberg, and Burgstall. At 220-470m altitude, the bedrock and topsoil ranges between mica schist and alluvial sand with numerous south and east exposures. Grapes are macerated up to 24 hours (depending on ripeness, with riper grapes receiving less time), then pressed over 6-8 hours, tank settled for a day and naturally fermented at 24˚C max and aged for 8 months in steel. Malolactic is inhibited by low temperatures, and the first sulfites are added at bottling. It\'s filtered but not fined. The residual sugar ranges between 50-70g/L, depending on the year.

Weszeli
Weszeli, Grüner Veltliner, Ried Kaferberg 1ÖTW
2019
0 cs
The Grüner Veltliner “Kaferberg” comes from numerous south-facing parcels at altitudes between 270-320m. Replanted in 1974 on limestone bedrock with clay and loess topsoil, the vineyards are sheltered from harsh winds. Each vintage is handled according to its growing conditions, but the general approach is to harvest each site in three passes: the first for entry-level wines and sparkling base, the second to provide blending components for the entry-level range, and the final (and most complex) for Erste Lage. Erste Lage fruit undergoes whole-bunch maceration for 6–18 hours—longer in cooler years, shorter in warmer ones—before a natural fermentation of 2–3 months in steel. Malolactic fermentation may occur if sulfur is not added for an extended period, though it is not desired. The Erste Lage wines are then aged in large wooden casks for 2.5 years before bottling, and released 4–5 years after the vintage. The entry-level wines go through a much shorter process and are released the year after harvest season.
Weszeli
Weszeli, Grüner Veltliner, Langenlois
2023
0 cs
The Grüner Veltliner “Langenlois” comes from dozens of large, soft-sloping, terraced plots planted between 1986-2015 at 270-320m with many different exposures. The soils are a mix of metamorphic, igneous, and sedimentary rock, with their most notable feature the calcareous loess. Each vintage is handled according to its growing conditions, but the general approach is to harvest each site in three passes: the first for entry-level wines and sparkling base, the second to provide blending components for the entry-level range, and the final (and most complex) for Erste Lage. Erste Lage fruit undergoes whole-bunch maceration for 6–18 hours—longer in cooler years, shorter in warmer ones—before a natural fermentation of 2–3 months in steel. Malolactic fermentation may occur if sulfur is not added for an extended period, though it is not desired. The Erste Lage wines are then aged in large wooden casks for 2.5 years before bottling, and released 4–5 years after the vintage. The entry-level wines go through a much shorter process and are released the year after harvest season.

Erste Lage fruit undergoes whole-bunch maceration for 6–18 hours—longer in cooler years, shorter in warmer ones—before a natural fermentation of 2–3 months in steel. Malolactic fermentation may occur if sulfur is not added for an extended period, though it is not desired. The Erste Lage wines are then aged in large wooden casks for 2.5 years before bottling, and released 4–5 years after the vintage. The entry-level wines go through a much shorter process and are released the year after harvest season.

Vallelonga is 100% Nebbiolo from 25-year-old vines (2023) on a flat surface of yellow and orange volcanic marine sand (~75%) and clay (~25%) at 292m. La Lida comes from 30–40-year-old pergola-trained Erbaluce vines on a gentle slope of acidic morainic soil. The wine is neither clarified nor filtered.
